audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers give Rumble six of seven stages including first item and 2+ items, while whys[3] says the lane starts tipping to Kayle at 4-5 and whys[4] through whys[6] say she out-ranges him with no counterplay available to him.
audit.why: Packet levelChart reads Rumble / Rumble / Rumble / Kayle / Kayle / Kayle / Kayle. Kayle wins 54.46%; Rumble has no dash and no hard CC, so once she is ranged he cannot reclaim any stage.
audit.corrected: Rows 3, 4, 5 and 6 -> Kayle; rows 0-2 stay Rumble. Flipped in matched full/content pairs.

audit.why: Four spikes present and correctly sited: Rumble levels 1-3 (Danger Zone Flamespitter plus Harpoon slow), Kayle 6, Kayle first item, Kayle late.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole page tracks Scrap Shield as the matchup-defining cooldown and tells the player to bait it. Scrap Shield is a 6-second shield — it is back before a trade finishes, so baiting it accomplishes nothing. The genuinely decisive mechanic, Junkyard Titan's heat bar, is never used as a trigger: at 100% Heat Rumble Overheats and cannot cast spells at all.
audit.why: Riot's passive text states the Overheat lockout explicitly. That silence window, not a 6s shield, is when a Kayle with 550-range E and Nashor's steps up. Other numbers: Flamespitter 10/9/8/7/6s at 600 range, Electro Harpoon carries 2 charges, The Equalizer 130/105/80s.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d now key the step-up to Overheat and quote the 6s shield as the reason not to wait on it.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Equalizer lays a wall of flames across the ground and Kayle has no dash in her kit, but nothing on the page tells the player to hold Flash for the wall rather than for the damage.
audit.why: missingInteractions rule terrain-cuts-retreat. Kayle's only movement tools are Celestial Blessing's move speed and Flash; if the wall lands behind her, walking out through it is the death.
